doc.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

chapter: New York: Jazztet and sidemen years
title: Auditioning for Benny Golson's Jazztet
summary: A telegram from Golson brought him to New York, where the Birdland rehearsal turned out to be an audition he won.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: No, what happened is we went to the Five Spot and played with the Brothers, and then I came back to Rochester and we went back into The Pythod. And I got a telegram from Benny Golson. And he said he wanted me to come to New York and join the Jazztet. And Tootie Heath was the drummer with the ‘tet then, and Tootie was leaving. So, great, I says, that’s fantastic. So it was about a week or so before I had to join them. And so they threw me a big party and everything at The Pythod. And I told everybody I was going to New York. I left and went to New York, and the rehearsal and the first job was in Birdland. And they put me up in the Alvin Hotel. It used to be the Elvin Hotel was across the street where all the musicians, and you know, everybody stayed there. So the rehearsal was that afternoon. And I went over to rehearsal and I got there and there was about six other drummers standing out there. And it turned out to be an audition, you know? And I said, hey, wait a minute!
Well that wasn’t the normal way of doing things was it?
Well I don’t know. I thought I had the job. I told everybody I had left home, you know.
You couldn’t go back if you didn’t get it.
I couldn’t go back. Party cake, I mean, everything. So—
Well you certainly had an incentive to do good.

So we went into Birdland and the first thing Benny said to me, he saw me coming across the street, he says “ah, here comes the Rochester Flash.” But we went down into Birdland and we, everybody got a chance to play and run over the music and run through all those pretty tunes that Benny wrote. And they went in the back and they came out later and said “you got the job.”
Yeah, right. And that night was my first gig, that very same night.
